name: Lukey
tagline: He's been dripping for you since 1987.

romance_success.title: Head Over Heels Over Pipes
romance_success.text: Lukey moved out from under the sink and into your bedroom. He still makes plumbing jokes. You still laugh. The kitchen has never been drier; everything else has never been wetter.

romance_failure.title: Water Under the Bridge
romance_failure.text: Lukey dried out, wised up and moved into a condo with low-flow fixtures. Word is he's dating a hot tub. Your kitchen is fixed. Your heart is dripping.

friend_success.title: Pipe Dreams Come True
friend_success.text: Lukey is your best friend, emergency contact and Sunday brunch date (strictly platonic, extremely bottomless). He fixes every leak on the block for free and tells everyone you rescued him.

friend_failure.title: Drain-ed
friend_failure.text: Lukey left without saying goodbye. Sometimes, late at night, you swear you can hear a single drip. Just to spite you.

lines: *A spray of water, a gurgle, and suddenly there is a very large, very damp man standing in your kitchen.*
Well, well, well. Somebody finally came down here to check on my [pipes].
Name's Lukey. Lukey the Leak. I've been dripping under that sink since 1987, sweetheart.

choices.text: Who are you, and why are you WET?
Lukey, huh? You look like you could use a good... tightening.
Get out of my sink.

lines: My pipes? Copper, baby. Original install. They don't make 'em like this anymore.
*He flexes. Somewhere in the walls, a faucet sighs.*
Course, they've got a little problem with... holding it in.
Anyway. You gonna stand there, or you gonna get your hands dirty?

choices.text: Who are you, and why are you WET?
You look like you could use a good... tightening.
Get out of my sink.

lines: Why am I wet? Honey, I'm a leak. It's not a lifestyle, it's a condition.
Every drip you've heard at three in the morning? That's me. Trying to get your attention.
You: That's a little creepy.
Creepy? Nah. Persistent. Like a good plumber. Or a bad plumber. Same energy, different invoice.
*He grins. A single drop rolls down his beard and lands on his boot.*
Oh, I like you. Most folks just call a professional.
Careful though, darlin'. Once you start fiddling with my fittings, things tend to get... [wet].
You: Is that a threat?
It's a forecast. Ninety percent chance of me.
*His face falls. The dripping gets louder.*
Ouch. Okay. Cold water. I get it.
But I've been in this house longer than you've been paying taxes, kid. You don't just *get out* of a pipe.
Tell you what. Go poke around your new house. I'm not going anywhere. Literally. I'm plumbed in.
*He gives you a two-finger salute. It splashes.*
Hey hey, look who's back! Miss me? 'Cause I've been leaking for you.
Sit down, sit down. Not there, that's a puddle. Actually that's also a puddle. Whole floor's kind of a puddle.

choices.text: Tell me about yourself, Lukey.
I came back for the view.
I came back to call a plumber.

lines: Me? Simple guy. Born in a hardware store, installed by a man named Gary who did NOT read the instructions.
Thirty-some years under this sink. You know what you hear, under a sink? [Everything|secrets].

choices.text: That sounds lonely.
Gary sounds hot.

lines: The last owners? Fought every night about whose turn it was to do the dishes.
Neither of 'em ever did the dishes. I did the dishes. Badly. Wetly.
And the fella in the bedroom wall? Moody guy. Black clothes. He drinks everything I spill and writes poems about it.
Anyway. Where was I?

choices.text: That sounds lonely.
Wait. There's a guy in my BEDROOM WALL?

lines: *He goes quiet for a second. Just the drip.*
...Yeah. Yeah, it is.
But hey! Now I got you. And you've got a [wrench], right? Tell me you've got a wrench.
You: I have a wrench.
*He puts a wet hand over his heart.*
Be still my pipes.
Gary was NOT hot. Gary had a mustache that looked like it was trying to leave his face.
But he had firm hands. I'll give him that. Firm, confused hands.
*He wiggles his eyebrows. Water flicks off them.*
The view's better from under the sink, trust me. I've seen a LOT of ankles.
You: That's the least romantic thing anyone has ever said to me.
Give me time. I'm a slow leak, not a burst main.
A plumber?! Oh, sure. Bring in some stranger with a snake and a bad attitude.
You know what a plumber does to a guy like me? He *fixes* me. No more Lukey. Just... a sink.
You: Isn't that kind of the point?
*He looks at you with big, wet eyes.*
...Is it?
Malcolm. Black mold. Lives in the bedroom wall. Real drama queen. Writes sonnets about decay.
Between you and me, I think he only exists 'cause I can't keep my water to myself.
Don't tell him I said that. He'll write a poem about it. A long one.
Alright, that's enough emotional plumbing for one day.
Come back soon, homeowner. My door's always open. Well. My valve.
*Lukey is sitting on the counter. The counter is now also wet.*
So I've been thinking. Which, for a pipe, is a big deal.
If you fix me, I stop dripping. I get to be a guy. Just a regular guy. Dry socks. The dream.
What I'm asking is... when I'm dry, what are we, {player}?

choices.text: I think we could be something special.
You'd be my best friend. My wet... dry... best friend.
We're a homeowner and a plumbing problem.
If I fix you, Malcolm dries up too. Doesn't he?

lines: *He sets down a wrench he definitely did not have a second ago.*
Yeah? 'Cause I've been feeling a lot of pressure lately. Building up. You know.
You: Lukey.
Sorry. Sorry! When I'm nervous I make plumbing jokes. When I'm happy I make plumbing jokes. I AM a plumbing joke.
C'mere.
*He kisses you. It's warm and a little damp and tastes like copper and somebody's spearmint gum.*
*He laughs, big and booming, and slaps the counter. The counter splashes.*
Best friends! I love that. I've never had a best friend. I had Gary. Gary doesn't count.
We're gonna get brunch. Do pipes get brunch? I'm getting brunch.
...Right. Course. Plumbing problem.
*The drip slows. Somehow it sounds sad.*
You know, you're the first person in thirty years I actually wanted to see. Just so you know.
*He winces.*
Yeah. Probably. No water, no mold. That's just science, baby.
He'd hate me for it. But I think it'd be good for him. Fella's been damp and miserable for decades.
Fix me first, maybe. Give the poor guy a chance to dry out and see the sun.
Alright. Next time you come by, bring the wrench. The real one.
I think I'm ready to get tightened up.
*Lukey is standing by the sink with his sleeves rolled up, holding a wrench out to you, handle first.*
So. This is it, huh? Righty-tighty.
Anything you want to say to me while I'm still dripping?

choices.text: I want you, Lukey. Wet, dry, whatever.
I want you. ...But you've been kind of a drip lately.
You're my best friend. Let's do this together.
Let's just get this over with.

lines: *You fit the wrench to the nut. He puts his big hand over yours.*
Together, okay? On three. One... two...
*Thunk. Squeak. Silence.*
*For the first time in thirty years, the kitchen is completely, beautifully dry.*
...Huh. My socks are dry. {player}. My SOCKS are DRY.
*He picks you up like you weigh nothing and spins you around the kitchen.*
Come here, you gorgeous homeowner. Let's christen the dry floor.

v4_rs2.fxText: Some things in this house got very, very wet again.
lines: *Later. Much later.*
Best. Repair. Ever.
*You fit the wrench to the nut. He doesn't put his hand on yours.*
You know what? I'll do it myself.
*Thunk. Squeak. Silence.*
I'm dry now. Thanks, I guess. Funny thing about being dry: you start seeing clearly.
And clearly? You only ever wanted me for my fittings.
*He grabs his flannel and walks out the front door. It's the first time you've seen anybody use it.*
...Best friend. Yeah.
*You crank the wrench together. Thunk. Squeak. Silence.*
*The drip stops. Lukey looks down at his hands like they belong to somebody else.*
I'm dry. I'm a dry guy. A dry, best-friend guy.
You need me, I'm on speed dial. Leaky faucets, clogged drains, emotional blockages. Free of charge. For you.
Over with. Sure.
*You crank the wrench. Thunk. Squeak. Silence.*
*The kitchen goes quiet. Lukey flexes his dry hands and doesn't quite look at you.*
Well. That's that, then.
Hey, gorgeous. Need anything tightened? Loosened? I'm flexible.
*He winks. It is, for once, completely dry.*
Oh. You. Just came back for my good wrench. Don't make it weird.
Best friend! Brunch Sunday? I'm bringing a casserole. It's a little wet. Some habits die hard.
*Lukey glares at you, arms crossed, from beside the perfectly functional sink.*
Sink's fixed. We're done here.
